gaps.sentence: You ___ wear a helmet when you ride a motorbike — it is the law.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses strong obligation, often from rules or laws: must wear.

gaps.sentence: He ___ have missed the train — he left home two hours early.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' expresses near-certainty that something did not happen: can't have missed.

gaps.sentence: After three attempts, she ___ pass her driving test at last.
gaps.explanation: A specific past success takes 'was able to' or 'managed to': was able to pass.

gaps.sentence: You ___ pay for children under six — entry is free for them.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' expresses absence of necessity: needn't pay.

gaps.sentence: You ___ not be so hard on yourself — everyone makes mistakes.
gaps.explanation: 'Should not' gives gentle advice against something: should not be.

gaps.sentence: I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.

gaps.sentence: The medicine ___ be kept out of the reach of children.
gaps.explanation: Written instructions use 'must' for essential requirements: must be kept.

gaps.sentence: You have been travelling all day, so you ___ be exhausted.
gaps.hint: an obvious conclusion from known facts
gaps.explanation: A logical conclusion from known facts uses 'must': must be exhausted.
